source_text:
Οὐ ξένα ὁμιλῶ οὐδὲ παραλόγως ζητῶ, ἀλλὰ ἀποστόλων γενόμενος μαθητὴς γίνομαι διδάσκαλος ἐθνῶν: τὰ παραδοθέντα ἀξίως ὑπηρετῶ γινομένοις ἀληθείας μαθηταῖς.
τίς γὰρ ὀρθῶς διδαχθεὶς καὶ λόγῳ προσφιλὴς γενηθεὶς οὐκ ἐπιζητεῖ σαφῶς μαθεῖν τὰ διὰ λόγου δειχθέντα φανερῶς μαθηταῖς, οἷς ἐφανέρωσεν ὁ λόγος φανείς, παρρησίᾳ λαλῶν, ὑπὸ ἀπίστων μὴ νοούμενος, μαθηταῖς δὲ διηγούμενος, οἳ πιστοὶ λογισθέντες ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἔγνωσαν πατρὸς μυστήρια;
οὗ χάριν ἀπέστειλε λόγον, ἵνα κόσμῳ φανῇ, ὃς ὑπὸ λαοῦ ἀτιμασθείς, διὰ ἀποστόλων κηρυχθείς, ὑπὸ ἐθνῶν ἐπιστεύθη.
οὗτος ὁ ἀπ’ ἀρχῆς, ὁ καινὸς φανεὶς καὶ παλαιὸς εὑρεθεὶς καὶ πάντοτε νέος ἐν ἁγίων καρδίαις γεννώμενος.
οὗτος ὁ ἀεί, ὁ σήμερον υἱὸς λογισθείς, δἰ οὗ πλουτίζεται ἡ ἐκκλησία καὶ χάρις ἁπλουμένη ἐν ἁγίοις πληθύνεται, παρέχουσα νοῦν, φανεροῦσα μυστήρια, διαγγέλλουσα καιρούς, χαίρουσα ἐπὶ πιστοῖς, ἐπιζητοῦσι δωρουμένη, οἷς ὅρκια πίστεως οὐ θραύεται οὐδὲ ὅρια πατέρων παρορίζεται.
εἶτα φόβος νόμου ᾅδεται, καὶ προφητῶν χάρις γινώσκεται, καὶ εὐαγγελίων πίστις ἵδρυται, καὶ ἀποστόλων παράδοσις φυλάσσεται, καὶ ἐκκλησίας χάρις σκιρτᾷ.
ἣν χάριν μὴ λυπῶν ἐπιγνώσῃ, ἃ λόγος ὁμιλεῖ δἰ ὧν βούλεται, ὅτε θέλει.
ὅσα γὰρ θελήματι τοῦ κελεύοντος λόγου ἐκινήθημεν ἐξειπεῖν μετὰ πόνου, ἐξ ἀγάπης τῶν ἀποκαλυφθέντων ἡμῖν γινόμεθα ὑμῖν κοινωνοί.
thought_title: The teacher's authority and the Word's gift
orientation: The author is explaining to Diognetus why he, a disciple of the apostles, can teach the nations: the Word himself was sent and revealed the Father's mysteries to the faithful.
pass_a_gloss: I do not speak foreign things, nor do I seek unreasonably, but having become a disciple of apostles, I become a teacher of nations; I serve the things handed down worthily to those who become disciples of truth. For who, having been rightly taught and having become dear to the Word, does not seek to learn clearly the things shown plainly through the Word to disciples, to whom the Word (the Son of God, identified with Christ), having appeared, revealed them, speaking with boldness, not understood by the unfaithful, but explaining to disciples, who, having been reckoned faithful by him, knew the mysteries of the Father? For this reason he sent the Word, so that he might appear to the world, who, having been dishonored by the people, having been proclaimed through apostles, was believed by the nations. This one is the one from the beginning, the one who appeared new and was found old and is always being born new in the hearts of the holy. This one is the eternal one, the one reckoned Son today, through whom the church is enriched and grace, being unfolded, is multiplied among the holy, providing mind, revealing mysteries, announcing seasons, rejoicing over the faithful, giving to those who seek, for whom the oaths of faith are not broken nor the boundaries of the fathers are transgressed. Then the fear of the law is sung, and the grace of the prophets is known, and the faith of the gospels is established, and the tradition of the apostles is guarded, and the grace of the church leaps for joy. If you do not grieve this grace, you will know the things the Word speaks through whom he wishes, when he wishes. For whatever things we were moved to speak out with labor by the will of the commanding Word, from love of the things revealed to us we become sharers with you.

choices.why: Keeps the articular phrase as a title for the Word, preserving the temporal claim of pre-existence.
rejected: he who is from the beginning
the one who existed from the start

choices.term: ὁ καινὸς φανεὶς καὶ παλαιὸς εὑρεθεὶς
choices.english: the one who appeared new and was found old
choices.why: Preserves the paradox of the Word's manifestation as both new in appearance and old in reality.
rejected: new in appearance but old in discovery

choices.english: being born in the hearts of the holy
choices.why: Keeps the present passive participle to show the ongoing, repeated birth of the Word in believers.
rejected: generated in the hearts of saints

choices.why: Preserves the aorist passive of λογίζομαι as 'reckoned' to convey the divine accounting, and keeps 'today' as the temporal marker.
The passive of ἁπλόω suggests spreading out or unfolding, which fits the image of grace expanding among the holy.

choices.english: the oaths of faith are not broken
choices.why: Keeps the passive voice and the noun 'oaths' to preserve the covenantal language.
rejected: the vows of faith are not violated

pass_b_english: I am not speaking about things that are foreign, and I am not searching in a way that goes against reason. I became a disciple of the apostles, and now I am a teacher of the nations. I serve what has been handed down in a way worthy of those who are becoming disciples of the truth.

For who, after being rightly taught and becoming a friend of the Word, does not eagerly seek to learn clearly the things the Word showed openly to his disciples? The Word appeared and spoke with boldness. The unfaithful did not understand the Word, but the Word explained things to his disciples. Those whom he counted faithful came to know the mysteries of the Father.
For this reason he sent the Word, so that he might appear to the world. He was dishonored by his own people, preached through the apostles, and believed in by the nations.
This is the one who was from the beginning. He appeared new, yet was found to be old, and he is always being born new in the hearts of the holy.

This is the one who always exists, the one acknowledged as Son today. Through him the church is enriched, and grace, being unfolded among the holy, multiplies. This grace gives understanding, reveals mysteries, announces the seasons, rejoices over the faithful, and grants gifts to those who seek. Among them the oaths of faith are not broken, and the boundaries of the fathers are not overstepped.
Then the fear of the law is sung, the grace of the prophets is known, the faith of the gospels is established, the tradition of the apostles is guarded, and the church rejoices in grace.
If you do not grieve this grace, you will come to know what the Word says, as he wishes, whenever he wishes.
For whatever we have been moved to speak out with labor by the will of the Word who commands us, we become sharers with you out of love for the things that have been revealed to us.

problems.source_quote: ἃ λόγος ὁμιλεῖ δἰ ὧν βούλεται
problems.why: Greek says the Word speaks about whatever he wishes; English adds a mediator ‘through whomever he wishes’ not in source.
problems.fix: …the things which the Word speaks about, as he wishes, whenever he wishes.
problems.ruling: ἃ = 'the things which'; δἰ ὧν = 'through which [things]', not 'through whomever'. English mistranslates relative pronouns, adding a mediator not in source.

edits.old: you will come to know what the Word says through whomever he wishes, whenever he wishes.
edits.new: you will come to know what the Word says, as he wishes, whenever he wishes.

problems.quote: For this reason the Father sent the Word
problems.why: The relative pronoun οὗ refers back to the Father mentioned in the previous sentence ('the mysteries of the Father'), not introducing a new subject.
problems.fix: For this reason he sent the Word, so that he might appear to the world.
problems.ruling: Greek 'οὗ χάριν ἀπέστειλε λόγον' has no explicit 'Father' as subject; translation adds 'the Father' incorrectly.

edits.old: For this reason the Father sent the Word
edits.new: For this reason he sent the Word

fixed: The mistranslation about 'the Father sent the Word' is real: the source uses the relative pronoun οὗ referring back to the Father, so 'he' is correct.

problems.quote: The Word appeared and spoke with boldness. The unfaithful did not understand him, but he explained things to his disciples.
problems.why: Pronoun “he” could refer to the Word, Christ, or an unnamed teacher, confusing the reader.
problems.fix: Replace “he” with the proper noun (e.g., “Christ” or “the Word”).

problems.quote: the truth and the holy and incomprehensible Word
problems.why: The Son/Christ is given many different titles across sections; a first-time reader may not realize they all refer to the same figure.
problems.fix: Add a note at first mention that 'the Word' is the Son of God, identified with Christ.

problems.why: 'Reckoned Son today' is awkward and unclear; the Greek likely means 'designated as Son' or 'recognized as Son.'
problems.fix: Rephrase as 'the one acknowledged as Son' or 'recognized as the Son today.'

edits.old: The Word appeared and spoke with boldness. The unfaithful did not understand him, but he explained things to his disciples.
edits.new: The Word appeared and spoke with boldness. The unfaithful did not understand the Word, but the Word explained things to his disciples.
the one acknowledged as Son today

fixed: The pronoun ambiguity was real; replaced 'he' with 'the Word' in both instances.
The glossary issue was real; added a clarifying note at the first mention of 'the Word' in the gloss.
The mistranslation was real; changed 'reckoned Son today' to 'acknowledged as Son today'.

problems.why: Same divine figure called by different forms; reader may lose continuity.
problems.fix: Use 'the Word' consistently after first introduction.

problems.quote: They are attacked by Jews as foreigners
problems.why: 'Greeks' and 'the nations' may refer to same non-Jewish peoples.
problems.fix: Clarify whether 'Greeks' and 'nations' are the same group.

problems.quote: the grace of the church leaps for joy
problems.why: Personification reads oddly; 'grace' does not naturally 'leap for joy' in English.
problems.fix: Rephrase as 'the church rejoices in grace' or similar.

problems.quote: I am becoming a teacher of the nations
problems.why: 'Becoming' suggests incomplete process; likely means 'I am' or 'I serve as'.
problems.fix: Use 'I am a teacher of the nations' or 'I have become'.

edits.old: I am becoming a teacher of the nations.
edits.new: I am a teacher of the nations.

edits.old: the grace of the church leaps for joy.

fixed: The glossary issue about 'the holy and incomprehensible Word' does not appear in the provided English text; the English consistently uses 'the Word'.
The glossary issue about 'Greeks' and 'the nations' does not appear in the provided English text; the English uses 'the nations' consistently.
The mistranslation issue about 'I am becoming a teacher of the nations' was fixed.
The unreadable issue about 'the grace of the church leaps for joy' was fixed.

last_rejected.quote: and now I am becoming a teacher of the nations. I serve what has been handed down in a way worthy of those who are becoming disciples of the truth.
last_rejected.source_quote: γίνομαι διδάσκαλος ἐθνῶν: τὰ παραδοθέντα ἀξίως ὑπηρετῶ γινομένοις ἀληθείας μαθηταῖς.
last_rejected.why: Source has a colon linking the clauses: 'I become teacher of the nations: I serve...' The English drops the colon and adds 'now', slightly altering the logical connection.
last_rejected.fix: I become a teacher of the nations: I serve what has been handed down in a manner worthy of those who are becoming disciples of the truth.
last_rejected.ruling: Adds ‘now’ and splits colon but meaning unchanged

last_rejected.quote: The Word appeared and spoke with boldness, and though he was not understood by the unfaithful, he explained things to his disciples. Those whom he counted faithful came to know the mysteries of the Father.
last_rejected.source_quote: οἷς ἐφανέρωσεν ὁ λόγος φανείς, παρρησίᾳ λαλῶν, ὑπὸ ἀπίστων μὴ νοούμενος, μαθηταῖς δὲ διηγούμενος, οἳ πιστοὶ λογισθέντες ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ ἔγνωσαν πατρὸς μυστήρια
last_rejected.why: The relative pronoun οἷς ('to whom') links back to 'his disciples' at the start; the English splits into separate sentences, losing the grammatical connection that the mysteries were known by those same disciples.
last_rejected.fix: ...to whom the Word, having appeared, revealed himself, speaking with boldness, not understood by the unfaithful but explaining to the disciples, who were counted faithful by him and came to know the mysteries of the Father.
last_rejected.ruling: Breaks sentence but still links disciples to mysteries

last_rejected.quote: If you do not grieve this grace, you will come to know what the Word says, as he wishes, whenever he wishes.
last_rejected.source_quote: ἣν χάριν μὴ λυπῶν ἐπιγνώσῃ, ἃ λόγος ὁμιλεῖ δἰ ὧν βούλεται, ὅτε θέλει.
last_rejected.why: Source says 'Do not grieve this grace [and] you will come to know...' — a command/prohibition, not a conditional 'if.' The English turns a command into a condition, changing modality.
last_rejected.fix: Do not grieve this grace, and you will come to know what the Word speaks, through whom he wishes, when he wishes.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek uses participial ‘not grieving’; conditional rendering is accurate

polish.changed: Clarified the Word as the speaker and subject throughout, broke up the contradictory adjective chain about the Word, and made the series of abstract clauses about law, prophets, gospels, apostles, and church read as a coherent sequence.

notes.why: Who they are and why they matter is left implicit.
notes.fix: Briefly note they are the original followers of Jesus.

notes.quote: This is the one who was from the beginning, the one who appeared new and was found old, and who is always being born new in the hearts of the holy.
notes.why: Mixes contradictory adjectives, making the sentence unintelligible.
notes.fix: Simplify to “He is the eternal One, ever new in the hearts of the holy.”

variants.text: the Word appeared and spoke with boldness

notes.why: The Son/Christ is called by several different titles across sections; a first-time reader may not realize all refer to the same figure.
notes.fix: Briefly note on first use that 'Word,' 'Son,' 'child,' and 'only-begotten' all refer to Christ.

notes.quote: the boundaries of the fathers are not overstepped
notes.why: Obscure phrase; modern reader cannot tell what 'boundaries of the fathers' refers to.
notes.fix: Add a note explaining the likely meaning (patriarchal traditions or inherited limits).

notes.quote: Then the fear of the law is sung, the grace of the prophets is known, the faith of the gospels is established, the tradition of the apostles is guarded, and the grace of the church leaps for joy.
notes.why: Series of abstract clauses without clear subject or verb logic; reads as word-for-word gloss.
notes.fix: Paraphrase: 'Then the law inspires reverence, the prophets reveal grace...' etc.
